maya: Heads-up: hit a nasty edge-case in the Next starter. Streaming responses freeze when ephemeral auth rotates mid-request. Repro in starter template.

kevin: Can you sketch the flow?

maya: SSR page calls /api/edge which exchanges a short-lived token, then calls the JS SDK to open a stream. If the token TTL expires and our refresh runs, SDK retry reconnects using the old header value -> client never gets resumed chunks.

jules: Oof. Which client version?

maya: @redwood/sdk 0.9.2, starter checkout from templates repo. Vercel edge runtime. Python client doesn't exhibit this.

kevin: Minimal snippet from the starter: 
```
export default async function edgeHandler(req, res) {
  const t = await exchangeEphemeral(req.cookies.sid);
  const s = await redwood.stream({ model: 'redwood/fast-13b', prompt: req.body.prompt, token: t });
  s.pipe(res);
}
```

jules: Logs show rotation then retry uses previous token?

maya: Yep: 
```
[2026-03-22T12:01:01Z] ephemeral fetched id=e1 ttl=20s
[2026-03-22T12:01:19Z] rotated id=e2
[2026-03-22T12:01:20Z] retry attempt=1 Authorization: Bearer e1
[2026-03-22T12:01:20Z] stream awaiting data
```

kevin: Looks like the SDK closures captured the header at open time. Proposed fix: accept authCallback in client config that is invoked per-request and per-retry to fetch headers dynamically.

jules: Also add a dedicated test that simulates token rotation mid-stream and asserts the retry sends updated Authorization. Good to protect parity with python.

maya: Short-term starter workaround: exchange ephemeral key and return a pre-signed one-time URL to the client (or have client fetch a fresh token immediately before streaming). Not ideal for demo flows but reduces incidents.

kevin: I'll prototype authCallback API: { auth: async () => fetch('/api/ephemeral').then(r=>r.json()).token } and wire it into retry path. Keep backwards compat by falling back to static apiKey if no callback provided.

jules: If you can add a small example to the starter README and a snippet in templates showing authCallback usage, that will help onboarding. Also update the eval harness docs noting ephemeral tokens are not safe with long streams unless you use authCallback.
